newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE COFFEE ENDS MIXED AFTER SEPT/NOV GYRATIONS.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE COFFEE ENDS MIXED AFTER SEPT/NOV GYRATIONS.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures drifted around in tight ranges on Thursday and largely spurned the arabica rally which was driven by a perception of supply tightness, traders said.
London's September/November spread was again a focus of interest as the nearby differential bounced between discount and premium -- but in thin turnover.
Market sources said while LIFFE's revised grading criteria had caused an increase in robusta supply for the September position, ungraded coffees were still being hedged in the futures market.
"Even though there have been grading problems over the last couple of months, people are aware there are plenty of robustas around," said one trader.
Trade sellers pressured nearby contracts lower early in the session, despite opening calls for a rise in the market,but then prices regained some lost ground.
But the strength in the New York market provided the focus of interest for London traders, who complained of a general lack of activity in robusta futures.
"London is like watching paint dry...everyone's watching New York. It's shooting up," he said.
Benchmark September robustas closed down $1 at $1,644 after spending the session in a range of just $43.
November was $4 lower at $1,646 and overall volume amounted to a light 2,347 lots.

In fundamental news, temperatures in key Brazilian coffee regions are expected to fall over the coming weekend due to the passage of a polar air mass but no frosts are forecast, local meteorologists Somar said.
But long-term models point to another air mass which should reach the coffee regions on August 15/16 and lead to another cool period, possibly without cloud cover.
